Transform Linear Predictor to Response

Source: R/LPtoY.R
LP_to_Y.Rd

Converts a linear predictor to observed responses using canonical link functions from generalized linear models (GLMs). Supports univariate and multivariate distributions.

Usage

LP_to_Y(
  X,
  true_beta,
  family = "Normal",
  n_trials = NULL,
  std = NULL,
  shape = NULL,
  theta = NULL,
  cov_matrix = NULL,
  n_categories = NULL
)

Arguments

X

A numeric design matrix.

true_beta

A numeric vector or matrix of true coefficients.

family

A character string specifying the distribution family.

n_trials

Optional integer, number of trials for the Binomial family.

std

Optional numeric, standard deviation for the Normal family.

shape

Optional numeric shape parameter (Gamma, InverseGaussian).

theta

Optional numeric size parameter for the NegativeBinomial family.

cov_matrix

Optional covariance matrix for multivariate families.

n_categories

Optional integer, number of categories for Multinomial family.

Value

A numeric vector of responses (integer categories for "Multinomial"), or an \(n \times q\) matrix for "MultivariateNormal".

Details

Simulates responses from the linear predictor \(\eta = X\beta\) using the 'Julia' backend. The supported families and links (the same as in Y_to_LP() and Beta_estimate()) are:

FamilyLinkExtra arguments
"Normal"identitystd (default 1)
"Bernoulli"logit
"Binomial"logitn_trials (required)
"Poisson"log
"Gamma"log (mean \(e^\eta\))shape (default 1)
"Exponential"log
"InverseGaussian"logshape (\(\lambda\), default 1)
"NegativeBinomial"logtheta (size, default 1)
"Geometric"log
"MultivariateNormal"identitycov_matrix (required)
"Multinomial"baseline-category logitn_categories (required)

For "MultivariateNormal", true_beta is a \(p \times q\) matrix; for "Multinomial" it is \(p \times (K-1)\) and the last category is the baseline. GLM stands for generalized linear model.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (interactive() && requireNamespace("JuliaCall", quietly = TRUE)) {
  julia_ready <- FALSE
  tryCatch({
    JuliaCall::julia_setup(installJulia = FALSE)
    julia_ready <- TRUE
  }, error = function(e) message("Julia setup failed"))

  if (julia_ready) {
    set.seed(123)
    n <- 100
    p <- 5
    X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
    beta <- c(1.5, -2, 0, 0, 3)
    Y <- LP_to_Y(X, beta, family = "Normal", std = 1.0)
    head(Y)
  }
}
} # }
